summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease presented with worsening lower extremity ulcers, increased pain, and malodorous discharge. He had recently undergone dental work without antibiotic prophylaxis. Admission labs showed leukocytosis and mild renal impairment. A wound swab grew sparse Pseudomonas aeruginosa, sensitive to multiple antibiotics. Given his immunocompromised state and increased pain, he was treated with a seven-day course of IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Dermatology recommended enhanced wound care with Dakin’s solution and alternating topical metronidazole and gentamicin. Diarrhea developed during treatment, attributed to antibiotics; it resolved with loperamide and hydration. His infection markers improved, pain decreased, and wounds showed clinical improvement. He was discharged home with oral azithromycin, continued topical therapies, and close follow-up with wound care and research teams.
problems: Ulcer of other part of foot
Complications of transplanted organ, stem cell
